assignments.title: VR Activity: A Courtier's Walk
assignments.html:
VR ACTIVITY
A Courtier's Walk
Solo · one in-headset session
16 points · file upload or text entry
⚜ ❦ ⚜
Before you start

Finish both lessons and read both sources first. Your notes from each page are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the page, so open it before you write. Then write your answers and submit them in this assignment.

WHAT YOU'RE DOING

Louis XIV used a palace as a tool of government. In your VR headset you will walk through a reconstruction of a grand royal palace and watch how the rooms, halls, and distances arrange people around a king. Your task is to find evidence that the space itself helped Louis keep his nobles close and dependent.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED
▶
Your VR headset, charged and ready
▶
Your course page for this week, which lists the session link and the place to enter
▶
A notebook or open document for quick notes while you are in the session
▶
About 45 minutes in one sitting
HOW TO JOIN
Where to go: Open your immersive session from the link on your course page, then enter the location named there.
Solo or group: Solo. You do not need a partner.
If something fails: Write down what happened and use the help contact on your course page. Do not skip the activity.
WHAT TO DO, IN ORDER
1
Review first. Reread the sections of the lesson “The Sun King: Versailles and the Taming of the Nobles” called The Palace and The Daily Show. Remember that rank decided who sat on a chair and who on a stool, and that only the king could give pensions and offices.
2
Walk the route. Move through the space the way a nobleman would, starting at the entrance and working toward the king's own rooms. Take your time, and note how far you have to walk and what you pass along the way.
3
Stop at three places. Choose three spots where the design of the space seems to serve the king. At each one, capture a picture with your headset and jot a note about what you see.
4
Look for the audience. Pay attention to who is meant to be watching at each spot. Ask yourself who is supposed to feel small, who is supposed to feel honored, and who is supposed to feel watched.
5
Write your response. After you leave the session, write one paragraph of about 150 to 200 words that answers this question: How does the design of the space help the king control proud nobles, and what might it cost him?
WHAT TO SUBMIT

Submit your three captured images and your paragraph in the Canvas assignment. Use the images as evidence in your writing, and name which picture you are referring to.

Estimated time: 45 minutes

SUCCESS CRITERIA
☐
I walked a full route from the entrance toward the king's rooms.
☐
I captured three images that show different parts of the space.
☐
My paragraph uses at least two of my images as evidence.
☐
My paragraph connects what I saw to what I read about Versailles in the lesson “The Sun King: Versailles and the Taming of the Nobles”.
☐
I wrote in complete sentences and kept to about 150 to 200 words.
FACILITATOR NOTE

Teacher-facing. Before releasing this activity, add the session link and the specific location to the course page, and confirm that students have a way to capture images in their headsets. The instructions above are platform-neutral on purpose. Grade with the course rubric for VR activities: three images as evidence, a paragraph that cites them, and reasoning tied to the lesson.

quizzes.title: Module Intro: Louis XIV and Absolute Monarchy
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRO
Louis XIV and Absolute Monarchy
2 questions · survey · one attempt
⚜ ❦ ⚜
Essential question for this week
How absolute was Louis XIV's monarchy, and did it leave France stronger or weaker?
Instructions

Welcome to Louis XIV and Absolute Monarchy. This short check-in is not graded. Your answers help your teacher see where each student is starting, so answer honestly.

What you will be able to do

The Sun King: Versailles and the Taming of the Nobles

  • Explain how Louis XIV centralized power after the Fronde.
  • Describe how life at Versailles bound the nobles to the king.
  • Evaluate how absolute Louis's monarchy really was.

Louis XIV's Wars and the Revocation of the Edict of Nantes

  • Describe the major wars of Louis XIV and how his rivals united against him.
  • Explain why Louis revoked the Edict of Nantes and what the results were.
  • Evaluate whether Louis left France stronger or weaker.

discussions.title: Discussion: Did Louis XIV Make France Strong or Hollow It Out?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Did Louis XIV Make France Strong or Hollow It Out?
Louis XIV and Absolute Monarchy
10 points · threaded discussion
⚜ ❦ ⚜
Before you start

Finish both lessons first. Your notes from each lesson are kept in My Notebook, the button inside the lesson, so open it before you post. Then post your answer here and reply to one classmate.

DISCUSSION PROMPT

Louis XIV left France with internal peace, a splendid culture, a large army, and the biggest population in Europe. He also left heavy debts, a tax system that favored the privileged, and a talented minority that had gone abroad.

Take a position. Did Louis make France strong, or did he hollow it out? Support your position with at least two specific details from the lessons, and include one detail that points the other way. Explain why you weigh the evidence as you do.

Aim for about 150 to 200 words.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a detail from the lessons that they did not use. If not, explain respectfully where it falls short, and point to a detail from the lessons that supports your view.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
Criteria Substantive (full credit) Thin (partial credit) Missing (no credit)
Claim and evidence
5 pts		 Takes a clear position, supports it with at least two specific details from the lessons, and deals fairly with a detail that points the other way. Takes a position but gives only one detail, or stays general, or ignores the opposing detail. No post, or no clear position.
Response to a classmate
5 pts		 Answers a specific point in a classmate's post and either strengthens it with a new detail or explains politely where it falls short. Replies in general terms, such as agreeing or disagreeing without a detail from the lessons. No reply.
10 pts total
